title: A Fake Lost-Dog Photo Can Still Cost You Real Money
body:
In late October, the BBC reported on a scam making the rounds online: people using AI-generated images of "missing" pets, dogs and cats that were never actually lost, sometimes pets that don't exist at all, to collect reward money from strangers moved by the photos. https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXEFVX3lxTE13bXVhRHEzR0JfeDdrRldobzNmRUVQYS14X29PcG1zNms4N3o1MU5iOEVaY0pPU0JiTE9ZNUR0TzgtLXRubXFzdTEzMlpSaUVlUXpFYzQ2LXFBTzdn?oc=5

What makes it work isn't clever technology so much as a very old trick dressed up in new clothes: a picture that looks real, a story that pulls at your heart, and a request for money before anyone checks anything. The AI part just makes the picture harder to doubt at a glance.

The lesson isn't really about lost pets specifically. It applies to any online pet listing, a dog you're hoping to pair with another owner's, a cat someone says needs a new home, a playdate request from a stranger. The photo can be real or fabricated, the story can be entirely sincere or entirely invented, and there's usually no way to tell which from a screen.

That's the whole reason PetMatch is built the way it is. Listings are self-reported, nobody at PetMatch checks vaccination records or confirms a pet is who the photo says it is, and no money ever changes hands through the platform itself, no deposits, no fees, no reward collected on anyone's behalf. Anything you work out with another owner is between the two of you, which is exactly why the only real safeguard is an old-fashioned one: meet in person, see the pet with your own eyes, and don't send anyone money before that happens. More on how to do that safely is at https://petmatch.fit/safety.

AI is only going to make convincing fakes easier to produce, not harder. The reward money and the pet it's supposedly for may both be real, or neither might be, but a stranger you've actually sat across from, in daylight, with a real dog or cat in front of you, is something no generated image can fake.
